 Judgment

This criminal revision petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec. 397 of Cr.P.C. challenging the order dated.14.10.2024 passed by the III ACJM., Court, Bengaluru in Cr.No.249/2023, on the I.A.,
dated.14.10.2024 filed by the Respondent No.2 U/Sec.451 & 457 of Cr.P.C in respect of defreeze amount of Rs.18,49,200/- and to correct the defreeze amount of Rs.14,99,200/- the chit fund balance amount actually payable to the Respondent No.3/accused No.1/Yuvarajan, the Trial Court ordered excess amount of Rs.18,49,200/-, instead of actual payable amount of Rs.14,99,200/- which is excess of Rs.3,50,000/- and above which is not liable to be payable by the petitioner herein to the Respondent No.2 and for such other reliefs.
2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
On the basis of complaint dated.23.12.2023 lodged by the Respondent No.2 the Respondent RMC Yard Police, in turn have registered FIR in Crime No.249/2023 against the accused person/Respondent No.3 for the alleged offence punishable U/Secs.406, 420 of IPC.
The petitioner is a third party to the said Criminal case, and is not a party to the said Criminal Case in Crime No.249/2023.
The Respondent No.3 was one of the member of the two different Chit Fund Groups maintained with the petitioner.

The Hon'ble III Addl. CJM (3rd ACMM), Bengaluru issued summons to the petitioner in Crime No.249/2023, to appear before the Court on 01.08.2024, and to furnish the details and to give material evidence or to produce any document or other thing for the prosecution in respect of the Chit amount details of the Respondent No.3/accused No.1 maintained with the petitioner herein.

Accordingly,
with due respect to the summons dated.10.07.2024 received from Hon'ble Court, the petitioner herein represented by its Manager Mr.Srinivasan P., appeared before the 3rd ACJM (3rd ACMM), Bengaluru on 01.08.2024.

It is further submitted that, on 01.08.2024 is it learnt from the Court that, the Respondent No.2 had filed I.A. dated.15.03.2024 U/Sec.451 and 457 of Cr.P.C to defreeze the Account of accused No.1/Respondent No.3 maintained with the petitioner herein, the said I.A. dated.15.03.2024 was not served to the petitioner herein.
The the Hon'ble Court asked the petitioner if any objections is there from the petitioner to defreeze the amount of the accused.

Since the petitioner is a third party to the said case in Crime No.249/2023, has replied Hon'ble Court clear that, the petitioner has no objection to defreeze the total remaining balance amount of Rs.14,99,200/-, payable to the accused/Yuvarajan after deducting the commission amount and his default and penal charges and miscellaneous charges as on the date applicable as per the rules of the Chit fund since he is a defaulter, in respect to the 2 different chit groups and to that aspect petitioner had filed Memo dated.01.08.2024 the different chit groups of the accused which specified the deduction and the total balance amount of Rs.14,99,200/- payable out of the said two chit Groups.

That, with the Order dated.19.10.2024 passed by the Hon'ble 3rd ACMM Court, the petitioner herein has to bare a loss of difference amount of Rs.3,50,000/- unnecessarily, which is not in accordance with law, and not acceptable, by the petitioner herein.
That, the trial Court has erred in its Order and has mentioned payable Defreeze amount of Rs.18,49,200/- instead of Rs.14,99,200/-.

3. After observation by the learned III ACJM., Bangalore has passed the order dated.19.10.2024 is to be set-aside the impugned Order in Crime No.249/2023 and the matter to be restored on the following grounds :- (1) The impugned order dated.19.10.2024 passed by the learned 3rd ACJM.,
Bengaluru in Crime No.249/2024 is totally perverse, illegal, unlawful and bad in law and therefore the same is liable to be set-aside by this Court.

(2) The Trial Court has erred in its Order and has mentioned payable defreeze amount of Rs.18,49,200/- instead of Rs.14,99,000/- and totally perverse, illegal, unlawful and bad in law and therefore the same is liable to be set-aside by this Court.

(3) Inspite of bringing the true facts the Hon'ble Trial Judge and the Hon'ble Trial Court allowed the application dated.14.10.2024 U/Sec.451 and 457 of Cr.P.C without valid reasons, and now the petitioner is facing great hardship and inconvenience which cannot be expressed in any means, and therefore the same is liable to be set-aside by this Court.

(4) The petitioner have produced all essential documents with respect to the amount transaction done and it is very clear that, the petitioner is liable to pay only Rs.14,99,200/- when such being the fact, inspite of that the learned Magistrate failed to appreciate the same.

(5) The petitioner is entirely depending upon the account for operation of their business, day to day transaction, already suffered huge loss due to the case filing by the petitioner, the Trial Court ordered excess amount of Rs.18,49,200/-, instead of actual payable amount of Rs.14,99,200/- which is in excess of Rs.3,50,000/- and above which is not liable to be payable to the petitioner herein to the Respondent No.2.
(6) The petitioner submits that the petitioner have filed this petition belated due to personal inconvenience.
(7) The learned Magistrate have failed to consider the above said facts, circumstances and grounds and was pleased to pas the order on the application mechanically.

sentences.text: Further it is observed that Orders passed by the Trial Court in Crime No.249/2023 no rival claim is made for defreezing the said account.
The petitioner is complainant in this case.
It is mentioned in the I.O report that the said amount belongs to petitioner.
The petitions is the original owner of the same.
The petitioner undertakes to abide any of the terms and conditions imposed by this Court for release of aforesaid amount.
Therefore, it would be proper to release the above said amount to the interim custody of petitioner.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case if the application of the petitioner is allowed no hardship or injustice would be caused to complainant.
However, keeping in view of the apprehension of the learned Sri.A.P.P necessary conditions can be imposed.

Therefore, there is a indemnity executed by the Mr.Sathish A.Teli, who is owner of the said amount of Rs.18,49,200/- and also the Trial Court imposed certain conditions that Mr.Sathish A.Teli shall reimburse the value of the amount of Rs.18,49,200/- suppose to he has not entitled, said amount and also impose certain conditions.

Therefore, there is no error committed by the Trial Court while passing the order on the application U/Sec.451 and 457 of Cr.P.C in favour of Mr.Sathish A.Teli S/o. Late Ashok Teli in Crime No.249/2023 dated.19.10.2024 and also it need full- fledged trial, at this stage cannot come to conclusion that this petitioner whether entitled or not for Rs.3,50,000/- as prayed in the petition.
Therefore, the petitioner has not made-out grounds to allow the revision petition.
Hence my answer to the above point No.1 is in the Negative.
